name: Wienuss
editorial_article: "Wienuss" is an electronic track by the German duo Mouse on Mars, released in 2012 as the fourth track on their album *Parastrophics*. The track showcases the group's signature approach to sound design, characterized by intricate, glitchy percussion, playful synthetic textures, and a rhythmic fluidity that balances chaos and structure. Typical of the experimental electronic soundscapes prevalent in the duo's mid-career work, "Wienuss" exemplifies their ability to manipulate digital artifacts into catchy, almost pop-inflected structures without sacrificing their avant-garde sensibilities. Released through Monkeytown Records, the track is a testament to their long-standing influence on the IDM and experimental electronic scenes, reflecting the same innovative, forward-thinking aesthetic that has defined their discography since the mid-1990s. The track serves as a vital component of *Parastrophics*, an album that captures the duo at a point of creative renewal, blending intricate sound architecture with the spontaneous, fun-loving energy that has kept Mouse on Mars at the forefront of electronic music for decades. Its name, like many in their catalog, hints at their penchant for wordplay and the oblique, humorous side of their artistic persona. Artists Andi Toma and Jan St. Werner constructed this work, cementing their status within the Monkeytown Records roster.
